messages:
Ari K: running into a weird WSL2 devflow issue with redwoodctl. installed via brew on Windows+WSL, then redwoodctl login times out and credential helper keeps flapping.
Maya S: hmm, what error do you see?
Ari K: paste: 
```
$ redwoodctl login --profile dev
Error: credential helper: failed to store token: open /run/credentials/redwood.json: permission denied
attempt 3/3: Post "https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/device": EOF
```
Rohit: sounds like a mount/perm mismatch. Are you running the CLI inside WSL but pointing config dir at a Windows path?
Ari K: yes I symlinked ~/.redwood -> /mnt/c/Users/ari/.redwood to share profiles. I thought that was convenient but clearly racy. local-serve created sockets in /run and helper tried to write creds to the Windows side.
Maya S: we added a credential helper that prefers the platform native store but falls back to file. On WSL the helper should choose the linux store, not the mounted windows path. Bug.
Rohit: quick fixes: 1) avoid symlinking home config into /mnt/c; 2) set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/redwood (inside WSL) so all runtime artifacts stay in the Linux FS; 3) or run `redwoodctl login --no-helper` to force copy/paste device code.
Ari K: `--no-helper` allowed login to proceed but then local-serve couldn't read the token because it looked in the helper path. so I ended up migrating the config: `redwoodctl config migrate --from /mnt/c/Users/ari/.redwood --to ~/.redwood.local` and changing env. painful for newcomers.
Maya S: action: make the credential helper detect WSL and prefer the Linux side; also teach the installer to warn if ~/.redwood is a symlink to /mnt.
Rohit: also saw the short auth retry window here. CLI gives up after 3 quick tries; SDK waits a bit longer which would have rescued the EOFs on flaky corp VPN. we should expose env knobs for retries or align to SDK defaults.
Ari K: I hacked env: `REDWOODCTL_AUTH_RETRIES=8 REDWOODCTL_AUTH_BACKOFF_MS=400 redwoodctl login` and it finally worked after a slow post. but that's obscure.
WSL Bot: system note: WSL mounts have different permission semantics; creating sockets/files on /mnt/ can lead to uid/gid mismatches.
Maya S: proposed fix list: 1) installer: detect if ~/.redwood points to /mnt and warn. 2) credential helper: detect WSL and prefer Linux FHS paths. 3) CLI: add user-friendly hint when token write fails, e.g. "Permission denied writing credentials. If you use WSL with a mounted Windows home, set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR to a path inside WSL or remove symlink." 4) Align auth retry/backoff with SDK or make env vars first-class in docs.
DevEx Bot: created DEVEX-2212: "wsl: credential helper and config path detection; improve auth retry defaults and hints" (PR planned).
Rohit: I'll pick up the helper detection, add tests for symlinked configs and mount points. Maya: can you own the installer warning?
Maya S: yup. will add the warning + a tiny help blurb in quickstart.
Ari K: thanks — once I moved config into WSL root the login+local-serve worked. will update the onboarding notes for WSL users with the env knobs and `--no-helper` fallback. :+1:
